parts.gloss: she who is fit to sulk / she sulked

words.gloss: she sulked / she became fit to sulk

literal: "I thought [of you]," I said; "then, what did you forget [about me]?" saying, me she did not embrace, she sulked.
translation: I told her, "I was thinking of you." Immediately she asked, "What did you forget about me that you had to think of me?" and, refusing to embrace me, she began to sulk.
modern: "நான் உன்னை நினைத்தேன்" என்று கூறினேன்; "அப்படியானால் என்னை எப்போது மறந்தீர்கள்?" என்று கேட்டு, என்னைத் தழுவாமல் அவள் ஊடல் கொண்டாள்.
explanation: This couplet portrays a delicate and witty moment of a lovers' tiff. When the hero tries to show his affection by saying he was thinking of her, the heroine cleverly turns it against him. She reasons that one only needs to think of someone if they had forgotten them first, and asks what he had forgotten. Refusing his embrace, she playfully sulks, showing how even loving words can be turned into a reason for a sweet argument.
